hook_text: In April 1945, American and Soviet soldiers hugged on a river bank in Germany. Two years later, their countries were enemies.
clip_script: April 1945, the Elbe River. American and Soviet soldiers meet, shake hands and celebrate. Together they have beaten Hitler. But their leaders believe in opposite worlds. America: private business, free markets, elections. The Soviet Union: the state owns everything, one party rules, and critics disappear into prison camps. They had teamed up only because Hitler attacked them both. Now the old mistrust returns. The Soviet Union has lost about 27 million people and wants a wall of friendly countries. Communist governments take over Poland, Hungary, Czechoslovakia. In 1946 Churchill says an iron curtain has fallen across Europe. In 1947 America promises to stop communism spreading and pours about 13 billion dollars into rebuilding Western Europe. Stalin refuses the money for the East. The allies who won the war have split the world in two. The Cold War has begun.
visual_style: Soldiers shaking hands on a river bank; two symbols side by side, a market stall and a factory with a red star; a map of Europe with a dark line drawn from the Baltic to the Adriatic; crates of aid unloaded at a port; a world map splitting into two colours.
pacing: Warm opening, steady build of tension, a stark close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to understand how the tension between the Allies led to the Cold War.
